stories.title: Teachers’ holiday digital training in Kamuli
stories.excerpt: Teachers from schools in and around Kamuli built practical digital skills during the August–September school holiday.

sections.heading: Practical skills for everyday teaching
sections.text: The Giebink Technology Center at Township Primary School hosted a digital training programme during the August–September 2026 school holiday. Sessions focused on using technology in teaching and school administration.

sections.heading: From lesson plans to digital records
sections.text: Participants explored digital lesson plans, PowerPoint presentations, report cards and internet research. The training offered time to practise computer skills that teachers can apply in their daily work.

stories.title: Digital learning opens to the wider community
stories.excerpt: A community digital training programme launched in June 2026, beginning with a focus on young people and their business ideas.

sections.heading: A new opportunity to learn
sections.text: In June 2026, the Giebink Technology Center began a community digital training programme in Kamuli. Its first initiative focused on digital skills for young people.

sections.heading: Skills connected to local ambitions
sections.text: The programme was designed to help participants use practical technology skills to develop their business ideas. It extends the centre’s learning opportunities beyond the school community.

stories.title: Nabakazi Petralina: growing confidence with computers
stories.excerpt: A teacher from St. Mulumba Primary School shares how digital training changed her confidence and classroom preparation.

sections.heading: Starting with the basics
sections.text: Nabakazi Petralina, a teacher at St. Mulumba Primary School in Kamuli District, describes beginning the training with little computer experience. She learned to operate a computer, type and save her work.

sections.heading: Taking new skills back to school
sections.text: Her account describes using Word and Excel to prepare lesson plans and report cards, using email and finding information online. She plans to keep practising and share what she has learned with fellow teachers.

who_we_are.heading: Who We Are
who_we_are.name: EdFund Uganda Foundation, Inc.
paragraphs: EdFund Uganda Foundation, Inc. is a US-based 501(c)(3) private educational nonprofit dedicated to restoring historic education infrastructure and bringing new technology into the classrooms of Eastern Uganda.

Many schools built in the 1950s fell into disrepair or closed following the political instability of the Idi Amin era. With inadequate government funding to renovate these structures, EdFund’s school rebuilding work fills a critical infrastructure gap.
By supporting institutions such as Kamuli Township Primary School, which serves 2,500 children, EdFund connects improvements to school buildings with better access to education and technology.

chapters.label: Kamuli in 2020
chapters.title: Our Journey of Transformation
chapters.text: These photographs show Kamuli Municipality as recently as 2020: unpaved roads, animals sharing the main roadways and vendors selling goods along the edges of the main street. With more than 50,000 residents, Kamuli Municipality is the administrative centre of a district with a population of roughly half a million.

chapters.label: Changing streets
chapters.title: Progress on the Infrastructure though Challenges remain.
chapters.text: Government investment has improved infrastructure in recent years, and many streets in Kamuli Municipality are now paved. Yet poverty remains a significant challenge. World Bank estimates based on the 2019/20 household survey put around 42% of Uganda’s population below the then international poverty line of US$2.15 per person per day (2017 purchasing power parity).

chapters.label: The school funding gap
chapters.title: School buildings also need investment.
chapters.text: Public funding for school improvements remains limited. Older school facilities need substantial investment, and many buildings date from the initial school construction of the 1950s.

chapters.label: EdFund’s response
chapters.title: Rebuilding spaces. Opening opportunities.
chapters.text: EdFund Uganda Foundation stepped in to help fill that gap. Over the past 15 years, EdFund-supported work has helped rebuild classrooms and dormitories at Kamuli Township Primary School, serving 2,500 boys and girls in grades P1–P7.

editorial_notes: Photo dates, recent infrastructure changes, school-building dates and the 15-year work history are supplied by the client; source originals remain unchanged.
Population figures retain the client’s rounded description; UBOS 2024 reports 76,758 in the municipality and 540,252 in the district.
The 42% statistic is explicitly historical: 2019/20 household survey, US$2.15/day in 2017 PPP. It is not presented as the current poverty rate or current poverty line.
The categorical claim that the government has no money is edited to limited public funding.
